admiralty.origin: After the British Admiralty, whose great Sembawang Naval Base dominated this coast from the 1920s to 1971.

aljunied.origin: After Syed Omar bin Ali Aljunied, the Yemeni merchant-philanthropist who gave land for mosques, churches and hospitals in early Singapore.

ang-mo-kio.origin: Hokkien for 'red-haired man's bridge' — after a bridge associated with the British ('ang mo', red-haired people); a rival theory reads it as the tomato, the 'red-haired person's brinjal'.

bakau.origin: Malay for the mangrove tree that lines the nearby Sungei Punggol.

bartley.origin: After Bartley Road, named for William Bartley, a member of the Municipal Commission.

bayfront.origin: Descriptive — serves Marina Bay Sands and Gardens by the Bay on the bay's waterfront.

bayshore.origin: After Bayshore Road along the East Coast.

beauty-world.origin: After the Beauty World amusement park and market (1947), once the biggest bazaar in the west of Singapore.

bedok.origin: Among Singapore's oldest placenames (charted from 1604) — possibly from 'bedoh', the great mosque drum, or 'biduk', a Malay fishing boat.

bedok-north.origin: North of Bedok — one of Singapore's oldest placenames, possibly from the mosque drum 'bedoh'.

bedok-reservoir.origin: By Bedok Reservoir, a former sand quarry turned water body.

bencoolen.origin: After Bencoolen Street, recalling Bengkulu in Sumatra, Raffles' post before he founded Singapore.

bendemeer.origin: From Bendemeer House, the Whampoa estate renamed after the 'bowers of Bendemeer' in Thomas Moore's poem Lalla Rookh.

bishan.origin: From Peck San Theng (碧山亭, 'jade hill pavilion'), the vast Cantonese cemetery that occupied the area before the new town was built over it in the 1980s.

boon-keng.origin: After Dr Lim Boon Keng (1869–1957), physician, reformer and philanthropist of the Straits Chinese community.

boon-lay.origin: After Chew Boon Lay (1852–1933), whose gambier, pepper and rubber estates covered the Jurong area.

botanic-gardens.origin: After the Singapore Botanic Gardens (1859), the country's first UNESCO World Heritage Site.

braddell.origin: After Sir Thomas Braddell, the first Attorney-General of the Straits Settlements.

bras-basah.origin: Malay 'beras basah', 'wet rice' — cargoes of rice soaked by the sea were dried on the banks of the stream here.

bright-hill.origin: After Bright Hill Temple — Kong Meng San Phor Kark See, Singapore's largest Buddhist monastery.

buangkok.origin: From 万国 ('myriad nations'), the name of the former Bankok/Buangkok rubber estate.

bugis.origin: After the Bugis, the seafaring traders from Sulawesi whose schooners crowded the Rochor and Kallang river mouths in the 1820s.

bukit-batok.origin: Malay 'hill of coconut shells' ('batok') by most readings — folk legend prefers the 'coughing hill', echoing quarry blasts in its granite face.

bukit-gombak.origin: Malay — 'bukit' (hill) with 'gombak' (tuft or topknot), for the twin granite hills that crown the area.

bukit-panjang.origin: Malay for 'long hill', after the ridge that runs beside the town.

buona-vista.origin: Italian for 'good view' — the road was named around 1902 for its hilltop vista toward the sea.

caldecott.origin: After Sir Andrew Caldecott, colonial administrator; Caldecott Hill was the home of Singapore broadcasting from 1937.

canberra.origin: After Canberra Road in the former British naval base, named for Australia's capital city.

cantonment.origin: After Cantonment Road, where sepoy troops of the early colony were cantoned (garrisoned); the station sits by the old Tanjong Pagar railway station.

cashew.origin: After Cashew Road and the cashew plantations that once grew on these slopes.

changi-airport.origin: Changi is possibly named for the chengai tree; the airport opened on the reclaimed eastern coast in 1981.

cheng-lim.origin: After Cheng Lim Farmway, recalling the poultry farms of old Sengkang.

chinatown.origin: The heart of the historic Chinese quarter Raffles allotted in 1822 — known in Cantonese as Kreta Ayer, 'bullock-cart water'.

chinese-garden.origin: After the adjacent Chinese Garden (Yu Hwa Yuan), the Jurong Lake garden built in 1975 in northern Sung style.

choa-chu-kang.origin: A 'chu kang' was a river plantation district run by a clan headman ('kangchu') — this one of the Choa (Chua) clan.

city-hall.origin: After the adjacent City Hall (1929), where the Japanese surrender was signed in 1945 and Singapore's self-governance was proclaimed in 1959.

clarke-quay.origin: After Sir Andrew Clarke, second Governor of the Straits Settlements, who made the Singapore River quays the colony's trading artery.

clementi.origin: After Sir Cecil Clementi, Governor of the Straits Settlements (1930–1934), whose grand-uncle Sir Cecil Clementi Smith had also governed.

commonwealth.origin: After Commonwealth Avenue, named for the Commonwealth of Nations as Singapore moved toward self-government.

compassvale.origin: After the Compassvale estate, whose name recalls the compass bearings of the old survey plans.

coral-edge.origin: Part of the Punggol waterfront naming theme.

cove.origin: Part of the Punggol waterfront naming theme.

dakota.origin: After the Douglas 'Dakota' DC-3 aircraft that flew from old Kallang Airport — remembered also in Dakota Crescent.

dhoby-ghaut.origin: From Hindi 'dhobi' (washerman) and 'ghat' (river steps) — Indian dhobies once washed and dried laundry along the Stamford Canal here.

dover.origin: After Dover Road, one of a cluster of roads named after English towns.

downtown.origin: Descriptive — in the heart of the Marina Bay financial district.

esplanade.origin: After the Esplanade waterfront and theatres — the old sea-front promenade of colonial Singapore.

eunos.origin: After Mohamed Eunos Abdullah (1876–1933), father of Malay journalism and founder of the Singapore Malay Union.

expo.origin: Serves the Singapore Expo exhibition centre, opened in 1999.

farmway.origin: After the numbered farmways of the former Punggol pig- and poultry-farming district.

farrer-park.origin: After Roland John Farrer, long-serving president of the Municipal Commissioners; the park hosted Singapore's first aeroplane landing in 1911.

farrer-road.origin: After Roland John Farrer, president of the Municipal Commissioners in the early 20th century.

fernvale.origin: After Fernvale Lane and the old Fernvale estate.

fort-canning.origin: After the hill fort named for Viceroy Charles Canning — known to the Malays as Bukit Larangan, the Forbidden Hill of the ancient kings.

gardens-by-the-bay.origin: Serves the Gardens by the Bay, opened on reclaimed land in 2012.

geylang-bahru.origin: 'New Geylang' — Geylang itself is often traced to Malay 'kilang', the mills that pressed coconut and lemongrass oil.

great-world.origin: After the Great World amusement park, one of the three famous 'Worlds' of mid-century Singapore nightlife.

gul-circle.origin: After Gul Circle, from Tanjong Gul at the western tip of the mainland.

harbourfront.origin: Descriptive — at Keppel Harbour, on the site of the former World Trade Centre; gateway to Sentosa.

havelock.origin: After General Sir Henry Havelock, British commander of the Indian Rebellion of 1857.

haw-par-villa.origin: After the Haw Par Villa gardens of Chinese mythology, built in 1937 by the Tiger Balm brothers Aw Boon Haw and Aw Boon Par.

hillview.origin: After Hillview Avenue, in the shadow of Bukit Timah hill.

holland-village.origin: After Hugh Holland, an early architect and amateur actor — not the Netherlands, despite the district's expatriate flavour.

hougang.origin: Teochew for 'river's end' (后港) — the upper reaches of the Serangoon River, heart of Teochew rural Singapore.

hume.origin: After Hume Avenue, named for Hume Industries, whose pipe factory stood here.

jalan-besar.origin: Malay for 'big road' — the avenue laid across a betel-nut plantation in the 1880s.

joo-koon.origin: After Joo Koon Circle in the Jurong industrial estate.

jurong-east.origin: Jurong is possibly from Malay 'jerung' (shark) or 'penjuru' (corner/cape); the fishing river became Singapore's great industrial estate from 1961.

kallang.origin: After the Kallang River and the Orang Kallang, the sea people who lived at its mouth before 1819.

kangkar.origin: Teochew 'foot of the port' (港脚) — the old Kangkar fishing village stood at the head of the Serangoon River.

katong-park.origin: Katong is popularly said to be an extinct species of sea turtle, or the shimmer of heat haze on the sea; the park sits on the old seafront.

keat-hong.origin: After the old Keat Hong village and camp.

kent-ridge.origin: Renamed from Pasir Panjang Ridge after the Duchess of Kent's 1952 visit; site of the fierce WWII Battle of Pasir Panjang.

keppel.origin: After Admiral Henry Keppel, who charted the deep-water New Harbour; it was renamed Keppel Harbour in his honour in 1900.

khatib.origin: From nearby Sungei Khatib Bongsu, recalling a khatib (mosque preacher) who once owned land by the river.

king-albert-park.origin: After King Albert I of Belgium, honoured as a WWI ally.

kovan.origin: After Kovan Road in the old Hougang countryside.

kranji.origin: After the kranji tree (Dialium indum), a hardwood once common along Sungei Kranji.

kupang.origin: Malay for the green mussel, harvested along the Punggol coast.

labrador-park.origin: After Labrador Park and its colonial coastal battery; the name descends from the 19th-century Labrador Villa estate.

lakeside.origin: Descriptive — on the western shore of Jurong Lake.

lavender.origin: Named in irony — Lavender Street was infamous for the stench of its nightsoil-fertilised vegetable farms, so residents called it after the fragrant plant.

lentor.origin: After Lentor Avenue and the surrounding estate.

little-india.origin: The historic Indian quarter that grew along Serangoon Road's cattle yards and spice gardens.

lorong-chuan.origin: Malay 'lorong' (lane) joined to the Chinese estate name Chuan.

macpherson.origin: After Lt-Col Ronald MacPherson, first Colonial Secretary of the Straits Settlements, designer of St Andrew's Cathedral.

marina-bay.origin: Descriptive name for the bay created by reclaiming Marina South and Marina East from the sea.

marina-south-pier.origin: Serves the pier from which ferries leave for the Southern Islands.

marine-parade.origin: After the seafront estate built entirely on reclaimed land in the 1970s.

marine-terrace.origin: After the Marine Parade estate street of the same name.

marsiling.origin: From Ma Xi Ling (马西岭), the hill-village name carried here by early Chinese settlers.

marymount.origin: After Marymount Convent and its school, established by the Good Shepherd sisters.

maxwell.origin: After Maxwell Road, home of the famous Maxwell Food Centre.

mayflower.origin: After the Mayflower estate in Ang Mo Kio.

meridian.origin: Part of the Punggol waterfront naming theme.

mountbatten.origin: After Lord Louis Mountbatten, Supreme Allied Commander in South East Asia, who accepted the Japanese surrender in Singapore in 1945.

napier.origin: After Napier Road, named for William Napier, Singapore's first Law Agent.

newton.origin: After Newton Road and Newton Circus, commemorating a 19th-century municipal engineer named Newton.

nibong.origin: Malay for the nibong palm of the mangrove coast.

nicoll-highway.origin: After Sir John Nicoll, Governor of Singapore (1952–1955).

novena.origin: After the Church of St Alphonsus nearby, universally known as Novena Church for its popular weekly novena devotions.

oasis.origin: Part of the Punggol waterfront naming theme.

one-north.origin: Named for Singapore's latitude — one degree north of the equator — as the research district's forward-looking brand.

orchard.origin: After Orchard Road, which in the 1830s ran between nutmeg orchards and pepper plantations.

orchard-boulevard.origin: Descriptive — on the boulevard running parallel to Orchard Road.

outram-park.origin: After Sir James Outram (1803–1863), British general of the Indian Rebellion of 1857.

pasir-panjang.origin: Malay for 'long sand' — the long beach that ran along the coast before land reclamation.

pasir-ris.origin: Malay, usually read as 'pasir hiris' — shredded / narrow sand — after the long sandy beach on the north-east coast.

paya-lebar.origin: Malay for 'wide swamp', after the marshland that covered the district.

pending.origin: Malay for an ornamental royal belt buckle.

petir.origin: Malay for 'thunderbolt' — Bukit Panjang's LRT stops carry Malay nature names.

pioneer.origin: After Pioneer Road and Pioneer Sector, honouring the industrial pioneers of Jurong.

potong-pasir.origin: Malay for 'cut sand' — the district was pocked with sand-quarrying pits before it became a vegetable-farming village.

prince-edward-road.origin: After Prince Edward, the Prince of Wales (later Edward VIII), following his visit to Singapore in 1922.

promenade.origin: Descriptive — by the Marina Bay waterfront promenade.

punggol.origin: Old Malay kampong name — 'ponggol' describes hurling a stick to knock fruit from a tree, and a riverside fruit wholesaling point.

punggol-coast.origin: Descriptive — serves the new Punggol Digital District by the northern coast.

punggol-point.origin: After Punggol Point, the northern tip where the old jetty and seafood restaurants stood.

queenstown.origin: Singapore's first satellite town, named in 1953 to mark the coronation of Queen Elizabeth II.

raffles-place.origin: Laid out as Commercial Square in 1824 and renamed in 1858 for Sir Stamford Raffles, founder of colonial Singapore.

ranggung.origin: After Lorong Ranggung; the ranggung is a marsh bird associated with the Serangoon area.

redhill.origin: English for Bukit Merah — the red laterite hill of the swordfish legend, in which a boy's clever plan to stop swordfish attacks ended with his blood staining the hill.

renjong.origin: After Lorong Renjong, an old kampong track of the district.

riviera.origin: Part of the Punggol waterfront naming theme.

rochor.origin: After the Rochor River and canal, one of the two streams that framed the old town plan.

sam-kee.origin: After the old Sam Kee kampong jetty on the Punggol shore.

sembawang.origin: After the sembawang tree (Mesua ferruginea), which grew along the Sembawang River; a specimen is planted at Sembawang Park.

sengkang.origin: Chinese 盛港, 'prosperous harbour' — recalling the fishing jetties of the Serangoon River.

serangoon.origin: Often traced to the ranggung, a marsh bird of the Serangoon River — or to 'di-serang dengan gong', 'attacked with gongs' to scare wild animals.

shenton-way.origin: After Sir Shenton Thomas, last Governor of the Straits Settlements, who endured the Japanese occupation as a prisoner.

siglap.origin: Malay 'si-gelap', 'the dark one' — legend ties the name to a solar eclipse, or to the darkness of its dense coastal groves.

simei.origin: Mandarin for 'four beauties' (四美) — the surrounding streets once bore the names of the four legendary beauties of Chinese history.

sixth-avenue.origin: After the Bukit Timah residential avenue of the same name.

somerset.origin: After Somerset Road, named for the English county.

soo-teck.origin: After the old Soo Teck kampong of the Punggol district.

south-view.origin: Descriptive — looking south over Choa Chu Kang.

springleaf.origin: After the Springleaf estate off Upper Thomson Road.

stadium.origin: Serves the National Stadium at Kallang, successor to the 1973 Grand Old Dame.

sumang.origin: After Sumang Walk; part of Punggol's kampong-heritage street names.

tai-seng.origin: After the Tai Seng (大成) estate name of the surrounding industrial district.

tampines.origin: After the tempinis tree (Streblus elongatus), an ironwood that once forested the area — one of Singapore's oldest recorded placenames.

tampines-east.origin: East of Tampines, named for the tempinis ironwood tree.

tampines-west.origin: West of Tampines, named for the tempinis ironwood tree.

tan-kah-kee.origin: After Tan Kah Kee (1874–1961), rubber magnate and philanthropist who founded Hwa Chong Institution next door.

tanah-merah.origin: Malay for 'red earth' — after the red laterite sea-cliffs that served as a landmark for sailors.

tanjong-katong.origin: The cape of Katong — the historic seaside district of Peranakan mansions.

tanjong-pagar.origin: Malay for 'cape of stakes' — after the fenced kelong fishing traps that lined the old shoreline.

tanjong-rhu.origin: Malay for 'cape of casuarina trees', after the rhu trees on the old shipyard point.

teck-lee.origin: After the old Teck Lee kampong of the Punggol district.

teck-whye.origin: After Teck Whye estate and road.

telok-ayer.origin: Malay for 'water bay' — the original shoreline where immigrants first landed; Thian Hock Keng temple on this street once faced the open sea.

telok-blangah.origin: Malay 'telok' (bay) and 'belanga' (clay cooking pot) — the pot-shaped bay that was once the seat of the Temenggong of Johor.

tiong-bahru.origin: Hokkien 'tiong' (from 塚, burial ground) with Malay 'bahru' (new) — the 'new cemetery', in contrast to the old one at Chinatown.

toa-payoh.origin: Hokkien for 'big swamp' — the new town rose from what was once marshland and squatter farms.

tongkang.origin: Malay for the wooden lighter boats that worked Singapore's rivers.

tuas-crescent.origin: Tuas recalls 'menuas', a Malay fishing technique that lured fish under floating coconut fronds.

tuas-link.origin: Tuas recalls 'menuas', a Malay fishing technique that lured fish under floating coconut fronds.

tuas-west-road.origin: Tuas recalls 'menuas', a Malay fishing technique that lured fish under floating coconut fronds.

ubi.origin: Malay for 'tapioca' — the root crop widely planted here, especially during the war years.

upper-changi.origin: Changi is possibly named for the chengai tree; the station serves the SUTD campus.

upper-thomson.origin: After John Turnbull Thomson, Government Surveyor of the Straits Settlements, who laid the road north.

woodlands.origin: The wooded coast seen from across the Johor Strait; early travellers described the shoreline plantations as 'the woodlands'.

woodlands-north.origin: North of Woodlands, by the future Johor Bahru–Singapore RTS link terminus.

woodleigh.origin: After Woodleigh Close, which took its name from a colonial-era estate house.

yew-tee.origin: Teochew for 'oil pond' (油池) — the Japanese stored oil in the area during the WWII occupation.

yio-chu-kang.origin: A 'chu kang' was a river plantation district run by a clan headman — this one belonged to the Yio (Yeo) clan, who grew gambier and pepper here.

yishun.origin: The Mandarin form of Nee Soon — after Lim Nee Soon (1879–1936), the 'Pineapple King' whose rubber and pineapple estates covered the area.
